---
title: "Mixed Model & BLUP Family (Frequency-based)"
---

::: {.callout-tip}
All four methods in this family solve the same mixed-model equations.
The only thing that changes is **K** — the matrix that measures
genetic similarity between individuals.

| Method | Relationship matrix **K** | Data required |
|--------|--------------------------|---------------|
| **PBLUP** | $\mathbf{A}$ — pedigree numerator-relationship matrix | Pedigree records |
| **GBLUP** | $\mathbf{G}_u$ — VanRaden Method 1 (SNP dosage) | SNP genotypes |
| **Microhaplotype-GBLUP** | $\mathbf{A}_h = \mathbf{T}_{\alpha h}\mathbf{T}_{\alpha h}^\top$ — Da (2015) | Phased microhaplotypes |
| **GWABLUP** | $\mathbf{G}_D$ — $\mathbf{G}_u$ re-weighted by per-SNP posterior probabilities | SNP genotypes + GWAS |

Same MME. Four relationship matrices.
:::

## Assumptions

The following assumptions apply to all four methods. Where an
assumption becomes more specific for a particular method, it is
noted in that method's page.

1. **Linearity and additivity.** Genetic effects act additively on
   the response scale. Dominance, epistasis, and gene-by-environment
   interactions are not modelled.

2. **Multivariate normality of random effects and residuals.**
   $\mathbf{u} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{K}\sigma_u^2)$ and
   $\mathbf{e} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I}\sigma_e^2)$.
   Shrinkage of GEBVs toward the population mean is a consequence
   of this distributional assumption — not an ad hoc regularisation.

3. **Independence of $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{e}$; homoscedastic
   residuals.** If residual variance differs systematically across
   families, populations, or sexes, a structured $\mathbf{R}$ matrix
   is required.

4. **K is correctly specified.** Errors in **K** — wrong pedigree
   entries, wrong allele coding, wrong allele frequencies — propagate
   directly into $\hat{\mathbf{u}}$ and bias GEBVs. There is no
   downstream correction.

5. **Method-specific requirements.** PBLUP requires complete and
   accurately assigned pedigree records. GBLUP and Microhaplotype-GBLUP require
   allele frequencies from the base (unselected founder) population.
   Microhaplotype-GBLUP additionally requires reliable phasing. GWABLUP requires
   a sufficiently powered training-set GWAS — an underpowered GWAS
   produces noisy weights that underperform equal weighting.

## General Linear Mixed Model

All four methods fit the same linear mixed model:

$$
\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{X}\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{Z}\mathbf{u} + \mathbf{e},
\qquad
\mathbf{u} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{K}\sigma_u^2),
\quad
\mathbf{e} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I}\sigma_e^2),
$$ {#eq-mm}

where $\mathbf{y}$ ($n \times 1$) is the phenotype vector,
$\mathbf{X}$ ($n \times p$) is the fixed-effect design matrix,
$\mathbf{Z}$ is the random-effect incidence matrix, and
$\mathbf{u}$ holds the additive genetic values (GEBVs).

Henderson's **mixed-model equations (MME)** solve for
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{u}}$ simultaneously:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{X} & \mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{Z} \\
\mathbf{Z}^\top \mathbf{X} & \mathbf{Z}^\top \mathbf{Z}
  + \mathbf{K}^{-1} \lambda
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{b}} \\ \hat{\mathbf{u}} \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{y} \\
  \mathbf{Z}^\top \mathbf{y} \end{bmatrix},
\quad
\lambda = \frac{\sigma_e^2}{\sigma_u^2}.
$$ {#eq-mme}

**What BLUP does.** The MME solves two problems at once. It estimates
fixed effects $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ while accounting for the fact that
relatives are not independent observations. It also predicts the
random genetic effects $\hat{\mathbf{u}}$ — the GEBVs — by
*shrinking* each individual's raw performance toward the population
mean. The amount of shrinkage is controlled by $\lambda$: animals
with few records or distant relatives are shrunk more; animals with
many close relatives and many records are shrunk less. High
heritability (small $\lambda$) means less shrinkage; low heritability
(large $\lambda$) means more.

**K as a common language.** The relationship matrix **K** tells the
MME how much information to borrow from relatives when predicting a
given individual. A large off-diagonal $K_{ij}$ means the model
transfers information from individual $j$ to predict individual $i$.
Choosing different **K** matrices — pedigree, genomic,
haplotype-weighted, GWAS-weighted — is a statement about which
definition of genetic similarity best captures the architecture of
the trait.

## Variance Component & h²

The MME requires $\lambda = \sigma_e^2/\sigma_u^2$, but these
variance components are unknown and must be estimated from the data.
`masreml` uses **REML** (restricted maximum likelihood), which
maximises the likelihood of the data *after projecting out the fixed
effects* — ensuring variance estimates are not inflated by
fixed-effect degrees of freedom.

| Method | `method =` | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| Haseman-Elston regression (HE) | `"HE"` | Method-of-moments OLS; single-pass, no iteration |
| Expectation-Maximisation (EM) | `"EM"` | Monotone $L_{REML}$ ascent; guaranteed $\sigma^2 > 0$; slow |
| Average Information (AI) | `"AI"` | Newton-like; near-quadratic convergence; step-halving safeguard |
| HE-initialised AI-REML (HI) | `"HI"` | HE warm-start, then AI-REML — same estimate as AI, fewer iterations |
| Auto | `"auto"` *(default)* | $n \ge 50{,}000$: HE only. $n < 50{,}000$: HE → AI → EM fallback |

See [REML Algorithms](blup-reml.qmd) for the full derivation, pseudocode, and per-engine convergence criteria.

Heritability is estimated as:

$$
h^2 = \frac{\sigma_u^2}{\sigma_u^2 + \sigma_e^2}.
$$ {#eq-h2}

::: {.callout-note}
**Chip heritability.** When **K** is built from a SNP or
microhaplotype panel, $\hat{h}^2$ estimates the proportion of
phenotypic variance explained by additive effects *as captured by
the markers*, not the true narrow-sense heritability. If the panel
misses rare causal variants, $\hat{h}^2$ will be below the true
$h^2$.
:::

## When to Use

| Situation | Recommended method |
|-----------|-------------------|
| No genotypes; pedigree only | [PBLUP](blup-pblup.qmd) |
| Genotypes available; polygenic continuous trait | [GBLUP](blup-gblup.qmd) |
| Phased microhaplotype data available | [Microhaplotype-GBLUP](blup-gblup.qmd#mh-gblup-da-2015) |
| Non-infinitesimal architecture + powered GWAS | [GWABLUP](blup-gwablup.qmd) |
| Highly polygenic trait; weak or no GWAS signal | [GBLUP](blup-gblup.qmd) (GWABLUP collapses to GBLUP anyway) |
| Per-marker effects needed, not aggregated GEBVs | [Bayesian Alphabet](bayesian-alphabet.qmd) |
| Binary trait | [Continuous and Binary Trait](continuous-and-binary-trait.qmd) |
